newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS - Elf opens door to Sanofi merger.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Elf opens door to Sanofi merger.

text.p: French oil company Elf Aquitaine said on Thursday it wanted its pharmaceutical and beauty products unit Sanofi to find a merger partner to boost its profitability but that it was not yet in any talks.
A merger would be the latest in a wave of consolidation sweeping the pharmaceuticals industry worldwide.
Elf, which holds 53 percent of Sanofi, said in a statement it would not insist on keeping its majority stake but would stay an "important shareholder" in the health and beauty products firm.
"It would be desirable for Sanofi to move nearer other pharmaceutical laboratories, through a merger, in order to speed up its development and increase its profitability," Elf said.
Shares in Elf and Sanofi jumped sharply after the news. Sanofi was up 4.34 percent in early afternoon at 485.40 francs while Elf was 2.82 percent higher at 448.10.

Elf, which has been forging ahead with an asset disposal programme aimed at cutting debt, said the decision to seek a merger was taken at a board meeting on Wednesday at which it discussed the group's long term development plans.

Sanofi has long been cool to what it called "the logic of megamergers". Only last month it said it was not looking for a merger, such as an often rumoured link with Rhone-Poulenc U.S. drugs unit Rhone-Poulenc Rorer, because it wanted to grow through alliances.
While analysts said on Thursday that Rhone-Poulenc Rorer would be the most likely logical fit, a Rhone Poulenc official ruled out the company taking part in a drugs industry alliance.

"We are the seventh biggest drugs group in the world, we are the leader in the six therapeutic areas in which we are active, we have our hands full with the launch of new products and we are not interested at all in any alliance," said Rhone Poulenc managing director Igor Landau.
Other potential partners included Bristol-Myers Squibb of the United States and Roche of Switzerland.
Sanofi and Bristol have been cooperating since 1993 in the development and marketing of some drugs such as Clopidogrel and Irbestan.
An Elf spokesman said the company had not yet started talks with anyone over a Sanofi merger.

"We have announced that we are putting Sanofi in a position in which to form alliances," he said. "We are opening another window of opportunity so the company can grow more strongly but there are no negotiations in progress at the moment."
Sanofi said last month it was willing to participate in a prudent way in the restructuring of the pharmaceuticals industry through acquisitions.
The company made a first-half 1996 net profit of 616 million francs ($117 million), up 11 percent from the same period last year, on sales of 11.3 billion francs.
Sanofi's health activities centre around developing drugs to treat heart diseases, breathing difficulties, central nervous system problems and cancer.
It also owns such perfume houses as Yves Saint-Laurent, Nina Ricci and Van Kleef & Arpels in France, Krizia and Findi in Italy and Oscar de la Renta in the U.S.

Elf's announcement was the latest signal of change in the pharmaceutical industry. Earlier this month, German chemicals giant Hoechst which holds 57 percent of French pharmaceuticals group Roussel Uclaf, announced an 18 billion franc offer to buy out minority shareholders.

In a separate merger announcement on Thursday, Rhone-Poulenc said it would combine its animal health and poultry breeding activities with those of U.S. drugs company Merck and Co Inc to form the world's largest operator in the sector.
($1=5.258 French Franc)
